long_biography.plain_text:
Leigh-Jones grew up in North Wales and went to sea at 16. He later earned a marine-engineering degree and worked as a research associate at Newcastle University. He founded Kittiwake Developments, which made fuel-testing and machinery condition-monitoring instruments for commercial shipping and industrial customers. The group broadened its technical range by buying emissions-monitoring specialist Procal and acoustic-monitoring developer Holroyd. It also backed Krystallon, a marine exhaust-scrubber venture formed with BP Marine. Parker Hannifin acquired the entire Kittiwake group in 2012. Its operations then served commercial marine, oil and gas, power generation and defence customers across several countries.

After the sale, Leigh-Jones and his wife Sebrina established Luxury Simplified in Charleston. The business combined property investment, restoration, construction, sales and holiday-rental management. In its first years, the group acquired and restored more than 40 properties on the Charleston peninsula. Leigh-Jones now works through Bridge Charleston Investments and related property entities across South Carolina. Property development has become the centre of his business career, following the marine-technology enterprise that first established him as an entrepreneur.
